reviews.text: All the staff is wonderful, helpful and kind.

Friendly professional service from the front desk, back office and the doctors. Dr Woody was exceptional. My Shepherd had CCL surgery to her left leg. We were nervous but the staff and Dr Woody explained everything and put us at ease. And knowing you can contact them at anytime, is a big relief. My baby is now home and recovering!

We had an incredibly positive experience with ACCESS throughout a very difficult period with our dog, Xena. Over time, we made multiple emergency trips to ACCESS as her health became more complicated, and each experience with the team was consistently professional, compassionate, and reassuring. Then, during her final two days, when her condition declined and we ultimately had to make the heartbreaking decision to say goodbye, that same level of care continued.

Dr. Paravicini was absolutely wonderful. She was compassionate, patient, honest, and incredibly gentle with both Xena and us throughout the entire process. Kaitlyn was also wonderful and showed us so much kindness and compassion during an incredibly difficult time.

What stood out most was how consistent the care was every time we came in. The entire ACCESS team was professional, responsive, and respectful, and we always felt that Xena was being treated as an individual rather than just another patient. Even during stressful emergency visits, communication was clear and we felt like the team genuinely cared about her comfort and quality of life.

During Xena’s final two days, we never felt rushed or pressured. Everything was explained clearly, our questions were answered honestly, and we were given the space we needed to make an incredibly difficult decision. When it was time to say goodbye, the team made sure Xena’s final moments were peaceful, gentle, and dignified.

We will always be grateful to Dr. Paravicini, Kaitlyn, and the entire ACCESS team for the care they gave Xena over the course of her visits and especially at the end. They made an incredibly painful experience as peaceful and compassionate as it could have been, and I truly couldn’t have asked for a better team to care for her.
Good experience here. The service is good, the staff are friendly, and Dr Hadar is very knowledgeable and took great care of my Yorkie.
Cardiologist Dr. Cole is first class!

The staff here is incredibly caring and professional. While I hope I never have to take my dog to an emergency hospital again, if I do, this is absolutely the place to go. They made a stressful situation so much easier. Highly recommend!

I brought my dalmatian there under Emergency circumstances and was taken care of right away. I didn’t have to wait too long as they were very busy. It was a Saturday..  Thus far and my dog is still in the hospital, I’ve been very pleased with the doctors, the front staff of the desks and also the vet techs have all been very professional and also very empathetic with what everybody goes through when you go to a medical emergency hospital.
One of the best specialty animal hospitals in Los Angeles. The best cardiology dept. and a great ER as well.
We're utterly delighted to hear about your positive experience at ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospitals - San Fernando Valley. Thank you for sharing your feedback with us.
Have been here twice now, each time service was outstanding, staff was quick and professional. Highly recommend.
We are elated to hear about your positive experience at ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospitals - San Fernando Valley. Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback.

I took my baby Suga in for an emergency situation.  This is an extremely busy place. My only complaint is that I keep all medical documents for my animals so I am informed of their medical history.  Thats what I am waiting for as well as my detailed receipt for my records.
The care that Suga received helped me better understand what needs to be done for her kidney disease.  They gave me the prescription for her food and let me know what I need to do moving forward. It broke my heart when I had to take my Aunts dog Chicklet there to be put down.  I am so grateful I was able to bring my Suga Bear home. She is resting and doing well. Thank you Access.

Dr. Masterson saw our 8 y/o F beagle Violet for a neurological evaluation of her neck and shoulder pain.  The veterinarian and staff were efficient and professional, Violet is responding well to the course of steroids and pain management they prescribed.  Exceptional care in a compassionate environment.  If you need specialized veterinary treatment for your pets, consider Access first. Another family member is seeing their cardiology group for her terrier with similar success.  Thank you Access!

It's much too expensive for a place you take your pet to during an emergency because in the heat of the moment you think your beloved family dog is bleeding out and it was the closest emergency veterinarian. I was fortunate enough to have a close family friend guide me on what to say and do so we can simply stabilize him and take him to his regular preferred veterinarian the following morning. Saved us from paying nearly $3,000 to $400 for the bare minimum. His regular vet was only just a few hundred dollars more than their bare minimum price to get the complete care with meds and all. If they were car dealers, then they would be the type to swear that it's a must to have the undercoating on a car during a summer heatwave for the upcoming winter in a location that's considered a desert that suffers constantly from droughts. I do, however, give acknowledgement to those deserving. All the receptionists at the front desk were friendly, understanding, and the only positive part of the experience. Your finances person was extremely unpleasant and her face became undeniably disgusted when we told her that we didn't want all the unnecessary add-ons and acted as if we inconvenienced her to walk to the back to get a new a price quote. Being forced into a financial shakedown right after experiencing something horrific and still recovering from the shock seems like the worst time to take advantage of someone and that's exactly what it felt like. Value PETS over PRICE. Value LIFE because you can't take your measly little dollars when you die. Please go somewhere - ANYWHERE - else if possible. They don't deserve your business when they put money before your loved ones.
Very sweet and kind staff and vets. They get very busy, so be patient and expect to let go of some cash. But I trust them.

I went in because my cat has a severe infection and they hold him overnight to fight the infection ,
This is the best place to take your animal in case of emergency/surgery Doctors go above and beyond for your pets. If I would be able to rate more stars I will because it deserves it!

Access San Fernando is a lovely facility.  The staff is warm, and checked me in quickly.  They are a good team.  I feel my consult while it was thorough, was overpriced.  The additonal ultrasound that I originally came in for was almost $2,000.  It should not be that much in my opinion.  I will have to go elsewhere to have it done at a more reasonable cost.
Our beloved 15-year-old miniature poodle suffered a seizure. Staff is very caring. Very nice and the doctor that admitted her was really nice and compassion
We apologize for the experience you had at ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospitals - San Fernando Valley. Please feel free to contact us at (818) 887-2262 to discuss your concerns further.
Jeanine at the desk sucks. Won’t be back.

Recently put our 16 year old dog down at Access.  Very difficult for both my wife and myself.  The staff were very nice and professional.  The doctor that did the deed was very patient and compassionate.  My deepest thanks to the doctor for helping us through this difficult time.  Superb experience.
Friendly, professional and efficient. Our dog Astro was well taken care of.

Our cat Max received the best care while at Access!  Our doctor was Dr. Escobar and he took care of Max and explained everything that he would need going forward.  He was thorough and patient.  All of the staff was wonderful and professional.  We and our cat were definitely in good hands!

Staff does a great job, but unfortunately our dog 🐕 has had the worst diarrhea ever non-stop since our visit and we still have not heard back from anyone. Also, I’d highly advise having dog 🐕 insurance, as it’s very expensive. …
They are wonderful, thinking about your animals not your pocket. best service, best people highly recommend.
Excellent experience staff. Very helpful. Best ER ever!!!!!!

I've driven by this facility for many years. Since I've been to other emergency hospitals near by in recent years with no pleasant experience, I hesitated to visit it until I recently had an emergency with one of my pets. I'm glad I made the decision to come by. Unfortunately my pet didn't make it, but I feel that I received an honest answer which helped me make the correct decision for my pet to peacefully cross the rainbow.
With my current pet, I had visited other 3 animal clinics for the same issue: a constant diarrhea that was severely dehydrating my pet. I'm happy I made the decision of bringing her to Urgent Care. Dr. Serex suggested a different approach to treat the diarrhea. She's doing better.
Anyone with an pet emergency, I highly recommend this hospital.

Had to use them twice: Once for a bowel blockage for my husky (10k) and now for town ACLs both back legs ($9k). Look, surgery for animals is expensive. But this place has given us fantastic surgeries & at least cost. How do I know? Because this was the SECOND bowel surgery and this one had no infection & she healed beautifully - unlike the first we had in Ventura. This place is in a horrible little mini mall with not enough parking. Don’t let this detract you: The care is first rate - from the surgeons to the aides. They take your calls anytime because they are 24 hours/day. They are likable. Kind. And first rate care.
The service was good. The doctors were professional and helpful.

It is just a comfort to know that Access offers urgent care for pets. I had no idea that this even existed especially when your primary vet is on vacation or can’t get an appointment as soon as possible. Emergency vet clinics are 2 to 3 hours wait minimum and at least I got an appointment the next morning. My dog was in pain with severe ear infection and I needed a Vet as soon as possible. When I did get here and got to see the vet, they were efficient, courteous, knowledgeable and treatment was on time. And the vet was nothing but the best. Thank you Access!
ACCESS was just that.  The doctor and staff were extremely personable, knowledgeable, efficient, and the most important, truly cared for our dog before, during, and after surgery.

Thank you to the team at Access for all they do. What a tough line of work to choose. I bet every day is challenging. I’m so glad they’re there to take care of my special little man. They have helped us navigate a very challenging megaesophagus life together, staff like Dr Hadar and Kaytee are so helpful and fantastic at what they do.

Killed My Pet!!!   cannot recommend Access Specialty Animal Hospital or Dr. Elena Hadar based on my experience.

I brought my 16-year-old Bengal cat, Nova, to Dr. Hadar after she had already undergone blood work and an ultrasound at another veterinary hospital. I wasn’t looking to be told what I already knew—that she had kidney disease, a heart murmur that had already been evaluated by a cardiologist, and abnormalities on her ultrasound. I was seeking a specialist who would carefully review all of her records, explain the findings, and recommend the safest treatment options.

Instead, I left feeling that my concerns and my cat’s medical history were not reviewed. During the appointment, I asked why she wasn’t going over the records I had already sent. She told me information was password protected and that she couldn’t access it, yet treatment recommendations continued anyway.

I also explained that I am Buddhist and do not believe in euthanasia. I made it very clear that my goal was to keep Nova comfortable and extend her life for as long as possible. Despite that conversation, she wanted to give me information about euthanasia, which made me feel completely unheard.

Dr. Hadar prescribed Mirataz and Cerenia and also recommended Epakitin. I was concerned because my cat’s calcium levels were already extremely high, yet Epakitin contains calcium based even my AI said, don’t give it to her!!. That recommendation made me question whether my laboratory results had been seen?!

After giving Nova the prescribed medications, immediately she began foaming at the mouth. She then started vomiting blood, experienced seizures, and within about two hours she died in my arms. the medications prescribed at this appointment led to my cat’s rapid decline and death. Watching my best friend of 16 years suffer and pass away so suddenly was the most devastating experience of my life.

I spent nearly $450 seeking specialized care because I trusted that my beloved pet would receive careful, knowledgeable treatment. Instead, I was left with overwhelming grief, unanswered questions, and the belief that the treatment plan failed my cat. I also asked to speak to a manager. I waited 25 minutes in the main room another 15 minutes in a other room and no one showed so I left. Also, I don’t remember the girls name that came out to talk about the different things that were needed for my pet every time I try to speak, she would speak over me and I was like let me talk. I’m letting you speak and she still kept doing it. I should’ve gotten her name, but she was entirely rude and disrespectful the only nice people were the ladies at the front desk Hannah I believe is one of them. I’ll also be filing a complaint at the veterinary medical board with breeze
As usual the care at Access is great the docs are kind and compassionate and explain everything well.

They took my injured dog in immediately and began the process of healing him right away.  Vets explained all the issues and possible outcomes and hazards.   There is a bit of a wait until you get to see the vet but not that bad.   Very expensive.

My cat stopped eating and was lethargic. I was very worried and called them on a Sunday. They said to bring her in immediately. They took wonderful care of her. I was very worried as she had to spend a couple nights there until they figured out what was wrong. But they were amazing. They let me visit her and sent me photos of her every morning. She's home now and completely recovered now. Every one there is super kind.

We are beyond thankful for the Neurology team at ACCESS, for the care provided to our kitty. We were reassured by the quality of care and communication we had received from the team, at a very emotionally difficult time for us.

Dr. Gerlach, Dr. Masterson, and the Neuro assistant Amber were so amazing to work with. Dr. Gerlach and Dr. Masterson were exceptionally knowledgeable, compassionate, professional, and patient. Amber was thoughtful, caring, and handled our communication smoothly. They listened to our concerns patiently, and answered our questions with the outmost thought and consideration.

It was not just the price to pay to receive service. It was the constant support we felt from the ACCESS team that we are really thankful for. Knowing that our kitty was in capable hands and a caring team was extremely valuable and reassuring to us.

Our kitty’s condition stabilized under their care, and we are so happy to have him home. It would not have been possible without the care of the ACCESS staff all together. Thank you again!

We are grateful for your positive feedback. Thank you for sharing your experience with us, Edward.

Sincerely, 
Hospital Leadership
Shoutout to Vanessa, she helped me get my new adopted dog's neurology records seriously fast. I really appreciate her extra efforts!
Extremely expensive but very worth it. A step beyond a vet.

Brought my cat in at 1am for emergency FIP treatment. They got us admitted right away and immediately started taking care of my cat. The whole team was great, they provided tons of helpful information and answered all our questions-despite how late it was. The following days they kept in constant contact with updates on our cat’s status and progress. And even texted me a picture of our cat the following morning to let me know he’s doing okay. 10/10 would recommend bringing your pet here.

Your positive feedback means a great deal to us. We are grateful for your trust and support.

Sincerely, 
Hospital Leadership
These guys are really good. I brought my very sick kitty in last week and she is recovering nicely.

I just wanted to come here and leave the review that this team  from Access Specialty veterinary Hospital truly deserves.

They gave my dog the most beautiful, tender, and loving care. I was there throughout the night, and I watched how they treated not only my dog, but every animal that came through their doors. It was so comforting to see how much compassion they showed every single pet.

They were upfront with me every step of the way, explaining everything before they did it and making sure I understood what was happening. They treated my boy with such kindness and handled him so gently. They also showed me so much compassion during one of the most stressful nights I’ve had as a pet owner.

I truly felt they only recommended the tests that were necessary, and I never felt pressured into anything. That honesty meant so much to me.

Thank you to the entire front office staff, the technicians, and the doctors for the incredible care you gave my boy. And a very special thank you to Dr. Chavez. Thank you for treating him as if he were your own. I will always be grateful.
From the receptionist to the vet tech to the Specialty cardiology vet, we were treated promptly, kindly, and experienced great service for our dog, who had recently been diagnosed with heart issues.

A wonderful place with compassionate care. I took my 15-year-old dog there to be put to sleep; she had a regular vet who had diagnosed her with an enlarged heart but refused to euthanize her, insisting she would be better off on medication. Less than a month later, she was suffering from seizures and anxiety attacks and was in a terrible state. It felt inhumane to let her suffer—and I was already dealing with the most heartbreaking pain imaginable, having lost my best friend (a 25-year friendship) just a month prior, so losing my little companion was absolutely devastating. The staff didn't just help me through the loss; they showed such humanity. They gave me time to say goodbye to my baby, allowed me a moment alone with her after she had passed, and even sent a condolence letter. Truly one of the best places—if I could, I’d give them 10 stars!

My dog coughed up blood at about 6 a.m. one morning.  I knew he needed immediate care, but his regular vet was not open that early.  I had been to Access Specialty Animal Hospital in Culver City and liked them, but when I looked up how long it would take to get there it was 35 minutes - too long.  So I checked the Access Specialty Animal Hospital San Fernando Valley and it was only 17 minutes.  I'd never been there, but I figured it was the same owner and hopefully they were as good.  I wasn't disappointed.  From the second they came out to greet us (they thought he might have kennel cough and could not take him through the reception area) they were absolutely wonderful - from the first technician to the last - and I probably saw four of them - they were all sweet, kind, gentle with my baby boy who was scared, and lovely to me.  The same was true of the doctor, Cecilia Kong, DVM.

My dog is a 52-pound husky mix and is 14 1/2.  He's been doing well for his age, but now he had a cough that we'd been unable to get under control with his regular vet, and now he had coughed up blood.  More to the point, coughing so much during the day was exhausting him and making his life a misery.  Dr. Kong told me what tests were available to determine exactly what was wrong.  But having had numerous paw babies I also knew that I would not put this or any other dog who is 14 1/2 through surgery or chemotherapy.  I asked if, knowing that was there anything the tests could disclose that would change how she'd treat him after reading a report from his regular vet and getting a thorough history from me.  She was thorough, straight-forward, and told me what I needed to know.  Having taken extreme measures off the table, nothing the tests showed would make any difference.  She acted accordingly, giving me the medicine he needed, changing some of the medication he was already taking, and giving me the option of changing to a stronger medication and prednisone if the cough wasn't better in a couple of days.  We're still working on that cough, but today he's a little better and some of his happiness is coming back.  We will continue with the instructions we received from Dr. Kong and see his vet in about a week.  I'm very grateful for everyone who helped us in this emergency.

Dr. Medina's negligence and lack of humanity led to not only the most horrific experience of our lives but ultimately cause my dog to become paralyzed.

We brought our 12-year-old dog, Obi, to Dr. Medina after a referral from our primary veterinarian because of elevated liver values, loss of appetite, and a known liver mass that needed further evaluation. We also brought him in because he had been limping, and one of our primary concerns was having his back legs evaluated with radiographs.

Initially, Dr. Medina was professional and kind. However, before even examining Obi, the conversation quickly centered on his age, cancer, chemotherapy, and euthanasia. While we understood cancer needed to be considered, it felt like our concerns about his mobility were largely dismissed.

Obi stayed at the hospital for most of the day. We were specifically told he should be finished around 4:00 p.m., when the ultrasound technician left. We returned at that time as instructed, only to be met with comments about how "weird" and "funny" it was that we were there. During one of the most frightening conversations of our lives, we were repeatedly interrupted with jokes about our arrival, even though we had simply followed the instructions we were given. It was an incredibly insensitive interaction.

We later discovered that the radiographs of Obi's back legs—the reason we had specifically requested imaging—had never been performed. We were offered the opportunity to return, but by that point we had lost confidence in the care he was receiving and sought imaging elsewhere instead.

The most devastating part of this experience came after we left. We paid for expedited pathology because we were told the results were urgent. We expected that if the results confirmed metastatic cancer, a veterinarian would call us immediately to explain what they meant and discuss next steps.

Instead, we received a blank email. There was no message in the body of the email, no indication that critical results were attached, and no phone call. Buried inside the attached PDF was the sentence informing us that Obi had metastatic cancer and needed to see an oncologist immediately. We discovered this by chance while looking through the attachment. No family should learn that their beloved pet has terminal cancer this way.

When we called with questions, Dr. Medina was unavailable. We were told she could only communicate through staff members who were unfamiliar with Obi's case. Every question required another lengthy hold while someone tried to relay information back and forth. At the moment we needed guidance, compassion, and direct communication from the veterinarian managing our dog's case, none was available.

After obtaining the leg radiographs elsewhere, Obi's condition deteriorated rapidly and he became unable to use his back legs. This reinforced our belief that his mobility concerns should have been fully evaluated from the beginning instead of being overlooked.

We understand that medicine cannot guarantee outcomes, and this review is not about Obi's cancer diagnosis. It is about communication, compassion, attention to the concerns we brought in, and the way devastating news was delivered. We left feeling unheard, unsupported, and deeply disappointed in the standard of care we received. I sincerely hope this practice reviews how life-changing diagnoses are communicated to families, because no one should have to experience what we did.

UPDATE: I was lucky to have my dog receive treatment just before ACCESS changed ownership to private equity. Private equity monetization of vet practices has in many cases led to increased prices at many vet practices. Vets are often being pressured to upsell in order to meet monthly revenue goals. It is heartbreaking. I didn't experience this at ACCESS as my dog received treatment there just prior to ownership changes being fully implemented. Bless those vets for working with me while still providing excellent care. I don't know if the upselling business model is in place at ACCESS as it was something I didn't have to experience.
2020  started out badly as my little dog became deathly ill on January 1st, 2020. I was able to get him in to be treated at Access. The vets and techs saved his life. Yes, it was expensive but they worked out a plan for me so I could treat him at home once he was stabilized. I am grateful for the skill and kindness of all the staff, from the front desk, the vet techs and the vets who worked together to save him.

They took my dog in right away, then came to get me and took a long time explaining everything to me in detail. The price for the follow up visit was reasonable and I felt like my dog was in excellent hands.
Service is OK but expensive

We brought our frenchie Mawly in for suspected,  ow confirmed, ivdd. ACCESS was Quiet, friendly, and no real wait time. From the front desk to the exam room everyone was so caring and professional! The wait time was non-existent, which is refreshing when you’re worried. We didn’t have to wait around the exam room or waiting area while they didn’t X-rays.

I have to say they catch you at the most vulnerable time when your dog is sick and in pain. Really in all honesty you will do anything for your dog but at what cost. They come out with a bill that you can buy a car with and they expect you to pay it right at that moment.  A lot of things on that list I come to find out your dog doesn't need but in some cases you end up paying. That is taking advantage of the customer at a horrible time when your dog is hurting. Of course I know its a business but I do believe it's unfair to the customer as we just want our family dog to be better. Overall we were out thousands of dollars and ultimately had to put him to sleep as he wasn't getting better and after all that we still didn't know what was the sudden sickness he endured. They has to be a better way this process can happen, we are in 2026. That being said just be mindful when you go to these emergency pet hospitals. This has taught me a valuable lessen how they operate and now I'm very knowledgeable so if I have to go I'm very in tune and mindful so I won't be taken advantage of.

I had a really positive experience at Access. Going in we didn’t know what to expect. It was a Saturday and my dog suddenly had a spinal injury and we didn’t have a lot of options where to go. But we were so pleased with their care. They called when they said they would. I could always reach someone to talk to. And they treated my dog with care and performed a successful surgery on him. It was definitely super expensive — almost shocking… but we are so grateful for their care and help and I am eternally grateful to all the doctors who helped my Charlie.
The doctor and staff were very knowledgeable and took good  care of my puppy.

We had a very positive experience visiting this hospital. Our 14 year old cat suddenly fell ill so we urgently needed to see a vet even though it was midnight. We called around but all hospitals around us either couldn’t take us in or had long wait time. When we finally called Access, they told us to come right away with no wait time. We were relieved. They were true to their work and after 5 minutes of checking in, our cat Oreo was taken in to be seen by the vet. We stayed there till 5 in the morning because the veterinarian, Dr. Chavez, was busy drawing blood, providing IV fluids and throughout explaining to us our options. dr. Chavez was the best! He was patient with our questions, clear with his explanations, gave us options on how to proceed with our decision making and really took his time instead of rushing with us. The nurse that helped us was just as exceptional. We watched him show compassion to another couple that was there to put their fur baby to sleep. He sat down with us and explained how to give meds to Oreo. They gave us free medicated food to take home to help Oreo with is GI issue. The receptionist was also kind and respectful. We left the hospital exhausted but very pleased receiving the best care for Oreo. Oreo bounced back the minute we brought him home and he started eating and drinking and not crying of pain. His energy level increased as well so we knew the doctor provided what he needed. We highly recommend this place for an emergency. You will be in good care.

I took my cat in from side effects of chemo.  ACCESS seemed always on top of things, getting my questions answered in a timely manner and calling me whenever there was an update. Everyone seemed caring and sincere.  I went to visit my cat at around 9:30 in the evening two days in a row.  Visiting hours end at 10:00.  They were really busy both evenings but didn't turn me away.  They let me stay with her as long as I liked and checked in on me every 15 minutes or so.  They brought treats and food and other necessities and never pressured me to leave.
My cat recovered largely due to the great care she received there.

I have had several bad experiences with emergency vet hospitals  in the past (whom I shall not name).

ACCESS SFV is one of the good ones!!!!!
Fast appointments, fast surgery date availability, and the vet was very thorough in her explanations!
Staff is very friendly. The doctor was very thorough on the procedure my dog needed.

We have been using Access for a few years now. They have specialists that are there 24/7 for unexpected emergencies. Everyone is very professional and takes good care of our pets. I highly recommend them.

Recently my dog passed and they cannot be more caring and direct to the point. Thank you so much for taking care of my Brucie on his last days.
As soon as i walk in told them what happened they grab her and started working on her right away.
From the receptionist to the vet tech and then to the vet was a great experience. They explained everything to us.

Thank you for your 5 star review, Sanford. 

Sincerely, 
Hospital Leadership

Five stars are not enough to reflect the outstanding experience I had with this team. Everyone was friendly, compassionate, and supportive throughout the entire process. Dr. Chrystal Nguyen is amazing—she did an excellent job performing surgery for my dog's herniated disc. She kept me informed from day one and never failed to provide updates, which gave me great peace of mind during a very stressful time. Thanks to her expertise and care, my dog received the best possible treatment.

I am truly grateful and highly recommend them to anyone seeking exceptional veterinary care. Thank you to everyone at Access for your outstanding service, dedication, and kindness. I can't thank you enough for everything you have done for my dog and our family.

My dog was diagnosed with a heart murmur and was confirmed with the Access cardiologist.  They have the the specialty equipment and the doctor has the expertise to clearly evaluate the health care of our loved pets and they do their job well.  Thank you Dr. Sinkin.

I don't have any complaints. I feel the prices are fair. Get insurance if that's an issue. I love my dog more than my kids so I spare nothing  to keep her around longer.  Had an early appointment for all day testing. I got a room at holiday Inn the night before as I'm in Bakersfield.  They have all specialties there, exotics, birds, càncer clinic, neuro, ortho, GI,internal med, cardiology.  Place to go if you're crazy over your dog like me, and can drop a grand or two n not trip.
God bless your animal

We found our little dog Lady listing to the left, head tilted and falling down when trying to walk. Called ACCESS in Woodland Hills (we are in Ventura) and they said bring her right down. ACCESS was referred by the Pet Emergency Clinic in Ventura as they did not have a neurological staff on hand. The staff were great, the doctor and nurses were awesome and our baby is home and recovering. I highly recommend ACCESS for your specialty ER needs.
Definitely worth the drive to this Access location

Thank you for the 5 star review, Silvia! 

Sincerely, 
Hospital Leadership

The staff are amazing, empathetic and really supportive. I went in and left crying, a long few days I will both never forget and feel like it's all a blur. I will always remember, though, how sweet they were with my Wally boy. He was given so much love by everyone I saw him in contact with, and they did their very best to be honest about his condition, and give him the best final days support possible. In the end, I hope I never have to go back there under such circumstances, but I'm glad it was here where we got to sit quietly in a private room with blankets and cuddles, to say goodbye.
The gentleman cleaning the lobby was even kind and asked if my sick boy was afraid of vacuum cleaners, and refrained from using it while we were in the waiting room. They offer water and snacks, something you won't even be thinking about til you're sitting there and realise you haven't eaten all day. They really get that this is a family affair, and not just an "animal" or pet..
I'd highly recommend pet insurance, so you can take advantage of their services without looking at the price tag.

I went in to the ER with my German Shepard "Cody" and the care was EXCELLENT from the Doctor to the Doctor's Aid as well as the front office folks. The communication was very good and they kept me informed at every step of the treatment. I want to give special mention to Dr. Jung, the explanations of my pet's condition were clear and the Doctor spent a lot of time with me to answer all my questions. Even though they were busy, they made me feel as if my dog was very important. My father was a Veterinarian and I worked in his hospital when I was in college, so I feel I have some knowledge of good animal care, and everyone I interacted with at Access Hospital in Woodland Hills was professional and knowledgeable. My dog is an important part of my family and my best friend, so thank you folks for the great pet care and my girl "Cody" thanks you!
We're excited to hear about your positive experience at ACCESS. Thank you for sharing your feedback, Marcos.

Your support means a great deal to our team. We truly appreciate the 5-star rating.

Sincerely,
Management Team
Extremely overpriced, takes several hours for results and explanation, not even to resolve pain or address any symptoms. Front desk very unclear on time estimates. Avoid.

Worst hospital ever! My dog has an autoimmune disease and needed a prescription refill. The receptionist told us they were “too busy” to send out the medication and that we would have to wait a week if we really needed it. Absolutely unacceptable for a medication that THEY told us our dog needed.
